pages.text: Rock warms by about 25 K for every kilometre down, and the water in its pores is under pressure. The mud in the well must press back harder than that pore pressure, or the well kicks; but not so hard that it fractures the rock. Between the two, weight and speed on the bit decide how fast it cuts.
$(thing)Set$(): Bit depth, Weight on bit, Rotary speed, Mud density.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Overpressured pockets: the pore pressure varies by ±3%·d.

$(thing)Limits$(): Kick: formation fluid is flowing into the well; Lost circulation: the mud is fracturing the rock; The diamond cutters are burning (above 700 K); The drill string is buckling under the weight.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): The faster it cuts, the faster cores come up.

$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Formation temperature: T = T₀ + (dT/dz)·h$(br)Pore pressure: P_p ≈ ρ_w g h (overpressured below)$(br)Mud pressure: P_m = ρ_m g h$(br)Fracture pressure: P_f$(br)Rate of penetration: ROP ∝ W·N^0.7·e^(−c·(P_m − P_p))$(br)Bit temperature: T_bit = T + friction
